method: Package indexes read from each distribution's repository. The systemd-boot binary of each package was downloaded and its Authenticode certificate table read; an empty table is unsigned. shim_accepts is the result of sbverify --cert on systemd-boot with the vendor certificate extracted from the distribution's shim. shim_grub is yes when the same check passes for the distribution's GRUB, no when the distribution publishes no signed shim, unknown when the binaries were not inspected. Not checked: revocation lists, SBAT levels, security suites, and aarch64 except where a record says so.

AlmaLinux 10 and Kitten 10.shim_evidence: Authenticode certificate table (PE data directory 4) is empty in the downloaded binary => unsigned. shim-x64 16.1-4.el10.alma.1 vendor db (extracted from .vendor_cert) holds AlmaLinux Secure Boot CA + two expired AlmaLinux code-signing certs; an unsigned image matches none. Only GRUB chains to it.
AlmaLinux 10 and Kitten 10.notes: systemd-boot-unsigned only; GRUB verifies against the AlmaLinux shim

CentOS Stream 10.shim_evidence: Authenticode certificate table (PE data directory 4) is empty in the downloaded binary => unsigned. Shim vendor db = CentOS Secure Boot CA 2 + CentOS Secure Boot CA 8 (extracted from shimx64.efi); nothing signs systemd-boot.
CentOS Stream 10.notes: systemd-boot-unsigned only; GRUB verifies against the CentOS shim

Fedora 44.shim_evidence: Authenticode certificate table (PE data directory 4) is empty in the downloaded binary => unsigned. shim-x64 16.1-7 .vendor_cert = single cert 'OU=Fedora Secure Boot CA 20200709, CN=fedoraca' (SKI B2:80:C7:AE...).
Fedora 44.notes: systemd-boot-unsigned only; no signed package in release, updates or updates-testing

Fedora Rawhide.shim_evidence: Tested against the shim Rawhide publishes today (shim-x64 16.1-7): its .vendor_cert holds exactly one cert, 'OU=Fedora Secure Boot CA 20200709, CN=fedoraca' (SKI B2:80:C7:AE:6B:88:4E:0F:4D:2A:0D:87:24:C2:5E:AF:6C:65:C3:26). The systemd-boot signer's Authority Key Identifier is 72:04:3C:47:C9:DA:5C:9D:50:89:A3:E4:85:92:CB:85:CE:43:ED:EF (the 2025 CA), and `sbverify --cert <shim vendor cert> systemd-bootx64.efi.signed` returns 'Signature verification failed'. Rawhide GRUB 2.12-88.fc46 verifies OK against the same cert only because it carries a second signature by 'CN=kernel-signer' <- fedoraca 20200709; systemd-boot has only the 2025-CA signature. So it is Fedora-signed, but not accepted by the currently published Fedora shim (nor by the Microsoft UEFI CA directly) until a shim embedding fedora-ca-20250530 ships or that CA is enrolled in db/MOK.
Fedora Rawhide.notes: signed with the 2025 Fedora CA only; shim-x64 16.1-7 embeds the 2020 CA and sbverify fails

Fedora ELN.shim_evidence: Authenticode certificate table (PE data directory 4) is empty in the downloaded binary => unsigned. ELN shim-x64 16.1-5 .vendor_cert = 'OU=Fedora Secure Boot CA 20200709, CN=fedoraca'.
Fedora ELN.notes: systemd-boot-unsigned only; the signed Rawhide package is not in the ELN compose

openSUSE Tumbleweed.signer: CN=openSUSE Secure Boot Signkey (issuer CN=openSUSE Secure Boot CA)
openSUSE Tumbleweed.shim_evidence: Extracted .vendor_cert from shim-opensuse.efi (shim 16.1-4.2): 'CN=openSUSE Secure Boot CA' (sha256 fp 20:7C:5D:A8:02:26:97:33...). `sbverify --cert <that cert> systemd-bootx64.efi` => 'Signature verification OK'; same result for grub.efi from grub2-x86_64-efi 2.16-5.1 (same signer). Shim itself carries Microsoft signatures (read from binary): 'Microsoft Windows UEFI Driver Publisher' <- 'Microsoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011' and 'Microsoft UEFI CA 2023 signer' <- 'Microsoft UEFI CA 2023'. Not checked: the shim's vendor dbx (deauthorized list, 7566 bytes) and SBAT revocation level against this binary.
openSUSE Tumbleweed.notes: sbverify passes against the vendor certificate of shim 16.1-4.2

Ubuntu 24.04 noble.shim_evidence: Authenticode certificate table (PE data directory 4) is empty in the downloaded binary => unsigned. Ubuntu shim vendor cert (extracted from shimx64.efi.signed.latest) = 'CN=Canonical Ltd. Master Certificate Authority'; GRUB is signed by 'CN=Canonical Ltd. Secure Boot Signing (2022 v1)' issued by that CA and sbverify verifies it; no systemd-boot binary carries any signature.
Ubuntu 24.04 noble.notes: systemd-boot-efi is unsigned; no signed package in the archive

Debian 13 trixie.signer: CN=Debian Secure Boot Signer 2024 - 20425036 - systemd-boot (issuer CN=Debian Secure Boot CA)
Debian 13 trixie.shim_evidence: Extracted .vendor_cert from shimx64.efi.signed (shim-signed 1.51~1+deb13u1+16.1-2~deb13u1, shim 16.1): 'CN=Debian Secure Boot CA' (sha256 fp 07:96:46:97:4B:CE:09:B1...). `sbverify --cert <that cert> systemd-bootx64.efi.signed` => 'Signature verification OK'. GRUB (grub-efi-amd64-signed 1+2.12+9+deb13u4) is signed by 'CN=Debian Secure Boot Signer 2022 - grub2' under the same CA and verifies the same way. Shim itself carries Microsoft signatures (read from binary): 'Microsoft Windows UEFI Driver Publisher' <- 'Microsoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011' and 'Microsoft UEFI CA 2023 signer' <- 'Microsoft UEFI CA 2023'. Not checked: the shim's vendor dbx (5500 bytes of deauthorized hashes) and SBAT revocation level against this binary.
Debian 13 trixie.notes: sbverify passes against the vendor certificate of shim 16.1

Arch Linux.shim_evidence: Authenticode certificate table (PE data directory 4) is empty in the downloaded binary => unsigned. No distro-signed shim exists in the official repos to accept anything (extra/shim is described as unsigned).
Arch Linux.notes: the systemd package ships an unsigned binary; the official repositories have no signed shim

Gentoo.version: systemd 262.1 newest non-rc/non-live ebuild in tree (binhost has 261.2 / 260.1-r2); systemd-utils 262
Gentoo.shim_evidence: No distro-signed systemd-boot exists: signing is done locally with a user-supplied key (ebuild/eclass text). The shim Gentoo packages is Fedora's, which would accept a user-signed systemd-boot only after the user's cert is MOK-enrolled.
Gentoo.notes: built from source and signed with a local key only; the binhost builds systemd without USE=boot

Fedora Hummingbird.shim_evidence: Authenticode certificate table (PE data directory 4) is empty in the downloaded binary => unsigned. The image's shim is Fedora's shim-x64 16.1-7, whose .vendor_cert is 'OU=Fedora Secure Boot CA 20200709, CN=fedoraca' (extracted, see Fedora 44); the image's GRUB (Fedora 2.12-66.fc44) verifies against it, the Hummingbird systemd-boot has no signature at all.
Fedora Hummingbird.notes: systemd-boot-unsigned only, and the image does not install it; the image boots Fedora shim and GRUB
